questions.question: Which action best begins an investigation of why ice melts faster on one plate than another?
options: Observe the conditions and ask a testable question
Change several conditions without recording them
questions.explanation: Scientific investigation begins with careful observation and a question.

questions.question: A student wants to test whether light affects seedling growth. Which factor should be changed deliberately?
questions.explanation: Change the factor being investigated and keep other relevant conditions alike.

questions.question: Which statement is a direct observation?
options: The liquid became cloudy after powder was added
questions.explanation: An observation describes what was seen; the other statements make conclusions.

questions.question: Why do scientists repeat measurements?
options: To check consistency and identify possible errors
questions.explanation: Repeated readings help reveal unusual values and improve confidence.

questions.question: Which is the safest way to smell a substance during a supervised school investigation?
options: Put the nose directly over the container
Waft a little vapour towards the nose
Shake the container near the face
questions.explanation: Wafting reduces direct exposure; substances should never be tasted.

questions.question: A class records how long four paper helicopters take to fall. What is the measured quantity?
questions.explanation: The recorded time is the dependent or measured variable.

questions.question: Which tool is most suitable for measuring the mass of a small stone?
questions.explanation: A balance measures mass.

questions.question: A student writes, 'The plant grew 2 cm in three days.' This is best classified as:
questions.explanation: It reports a measured change over a stated time.

questions.question: Which question can be investigated by a fair experiment?
options: Does warmer water dissolve a fixed amount of sugar faster?
Is science more interesting than art?
Which food tastes best to everyone?
questions.explanation: It can be tested by controlling conditions and measuring dissolving time.

questions.question: Why should an experiment change only one main factor at a time?
options: So the effect of that factor can be judged fairly
So the experiment finishes without observations
So other factors can be ignored
questions.explanation: Changing one factor while controlling others helps identify cause and effect.

questions.question: A group tests three materials for keeping water cool. What should be the same in every cup?
questions.explanation: A fair comparison keeps starting conditions and other relevant factors the same.

questions.question: Which tool measures the volume of a small amount of liquid most directly?
questions.explanation: A measuring cylinder is designed to measure liquid volume.

questions.question: A student says a metal spoon feels colder than a wooden spoon kept in the same room. Which explanation is best?
options: Metal must have a lower room temperature
Metal transfers heat away from the hand faster
The spoon's mass changes its temperature
questions.explanation: Metal is a better thermal conductor, so it draws heat from the hand faster.

questions.question: Which is an inference rather than a direct observation?
options: The wet ground may mean it rained recently
There are water drops on the path
The path is darker near the tap
questions.explanation: The cause of the wet ground is inferred; the other statements describe observations.

questions.question: A student measures a leaf as 7.2 cm, 7.1 cm and 7.2 cm. Which is a sensible reported value?
options: 7.5 cm because it is the largest
questions.explanation: The repeated values cluster around 7.2 cm.

questions.question: Which item is a model used in science?
options: A photograph of a real mountain
questions.explanation: A globe is a simplified representation of Earth.

questions.question: A student claims that all seeds germinate faster in sunlight. Which evidence would best test the claim?
options: Ask one friend for an opinion
Compare similar seeds under controlled light and dark conditions
Choose only seeds that support the claim
questions.explanation: A controlled comparison provides evidence about the effect of light.

questions.question: Why is it useful to record observations in a table during an investigation?
options: It organises results so patterns can be compared
It removes the need to measure
It guarantees the hypothesis is correct
questions.explanation: Tables make data easier to compare and analyse.

questions.question: Which conclusion is best supported if a toy car travels farther on a smooth floor than on a rough mat in repeated trials?
options: The car always travels farther on every smooth surface
The rough mat adds energy to the car
The car's mass has become zero
The surface may affect how far the car travels
questions.explanation: The repeated comparison supports a cautious conclusion about the tested surfaces.

questions.question: A student tests four paper types for absorbency. What should be measured to compare them?
options: Amount of water absorbed under the same conditions
questions.explanation: Absorbency is assessed by measuring water taken up using a consistent method.

questions.question: A thermometer shows 26°C before an experiment and 31°C afterwards. What is the temperature change?
A hypothesis is best described as:
options: A testable possible explanation or prediction
A result that cannot be questioned
questions.explanation: A hypothesis can be tested using observations or an experiment.

questions.question: A student pours equal volumes of water into wide and narrow dishes. Which factor is being investigated if the time to dry is recorded?
options: Effect of dish material if both dishes are identical
Effect of exposed surface area on drying time
questions.explanation: The dishes expose different surface areas while other conditions are controlled.

questions.question: Which graph is most suitable for comparing the number of seeds that germinate in four different soil types?
questions.explanation: A bar graph compares quantities across categories.

questions.question: A result differs greatly from the other repeated readings. What should the student do first?
options: Check the procedure and repeat the measurement
questions.explanation: An unusual result should be investigated before it is excluded.

questions.question: A student places one ice cube on metal and another identical cube on plastic. Both start at the same temperature. Which condition must also be kept similar?
options: Size of the ice cubes and surrounding conditions
questions.explanation: The comparison is fair when ice size and environmental conditions are controlled.

questions.question: A fair test finds that a plant near a window grew 4 cm and one in a dark cupboard grew 1 cm. What can be concluded most carefully?
options: All plants always need direct sunlight
Light is the only factor affecting growth
Under these tested conditions, the plant near the window grew more
questions.explanation: The evidence supports only the comparison under the conditions tested.

questions.question: Why should a measuring cylinder be read at eye level?
options: To reduce reading error from viewing the liquid level at an angle
questions.explanation: Reading at eye level reduces parallax error.

questions.question: A student wants to know whether the length of a paper strip affects how much weight it can hold. Which is the independent variable?
options: Type of paper if kept the same
questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor deliberately changed.

questions.question: A class finds that seeds in moist soil germinate but seeds in dry soil do not. Which additional test would help check whether water is the reason?
options: Repeat with similar seeds and keep temperature and other conditions the same
Change seed type and light at the same time
Use only one seed in each group and stop
Add fertiliser only to the dry soil
questions.explanation: Repeating a controlled test reduces the chance that another factor explains the result.

questions.question: Which observation would be strongest evidence that a new material conducts electricity?
options: The material is attracted to a ruler
A complete circuit lights a bulb when the material bridges a gap
questions.explanation: A working circuit is a direct test of electrical conductivity.

questions.question: A student measures the same table with two different rulers and gets 120 cm and 121 cm. Which is the best response?
options: Add the readings to get the table length
Check ruler alignment and zero marks, then repeat
Assume the table is changing length
questions.explanation: Alignment and zero error can cause small differences.

questions.question: A class compares how far a marble rolls down ramps of different heights. Which quantity should be kept the same for a fair comparison?
options: The marble and the ramp surface
questions.explanation: Keep the object and surface consistent while changing the ramp height.

questions.question: A student states, 'The plant grew because it received more light.' What further evidence would strengthen this explanation?
options: Repeated trials with similar plants and controlled water, soil and temperature
A photograph of only the tallest plant
A statement from someone who likes plants
Changing light, water and soil together
questions.explanation: Controlled repeated trials help isolate the effect of light.

questions.question: A model of the solar system shows planets much closer to the Sun than they really are. What is a limitation of this model?
options: It cannot show that planets orbit the Sun
It proves planets are all the same size
It is the actual solar system
It does not show the true distances to scale
questions.explanation: Models simplify reality and may not preserve every scale relationship.

questions.question: Which statement best explains why a scientific explanation may change over time?
options: Scientific ideas are chosen by voting only
New reliable evidence can improve or replace an earlier explanation
questions.explanation: Scientific knowledge develops as evidence and methods improve.

questions.question: A student records the shadow length every hour. Which display best shows how the length changes over time?
options: A pie chart of classroom subjects
questions.explanation: A line graph shows change across ordered time points.

questions.question: A digital balance reads 0.0 g before an object is placed on it. Why is this check useful?
options: It checks that the balance is zeroed before measuring
It proves the object has no mass
questions.explanation: Zeroing avoids a systematic offset in the measurement.

questions.question: An experiment produces a result that does not support the hypothesis. What should the student do?
options: Change the data to fit the hypothesis
Repeat until the preferred answer appears
Report the result honestly and reconsider the hypothesis
questions.explanation: Evidence must be reported honestly, even when it does not support the prediction.

questions.question: A student compares evaporation from two plates, one in moving air and one in still air. What should be identical?
options: Water volume, plate size and starting temperature
questions.explanation: Those starting conditions should be controlled when testing air movement.

questions.question: A class wants to test whether darker surfaces warm faster in sunlight. Which measurement would best answer the question?
options: Temperature change of each surface over the same time
questions.explanation: Temperature change directly measures warming.

questions.question: A scientist reports an average of three readings. Why should the individual readings also be kept?
options: They show variation and allow others to check the calculation
They guarantee there was no error
questions.explanation: The raw data provide transparency and context for the average.

questions.question: A class wants to compare how quickly water evaporates from two dishes. Which plan isolates the effect of dish width?
options: Use equal water volumes, identical dishes except for width, the same location and the same start time
Use different water volumes and place one dish in sunlight
Use a wide dish near a fan and a narrow dish in a cupboard
Change dish width, water temperature and airflow together
questions.explanation: Only width should change. Equal volumes, location, temperature and airflow keep the comparison fair.
questions.difficultyRationale: The learner must identify the variable being tested and control the other conditions.

questions.question: Three teams repeat the same measurement. Their readings are A: 12, 12, 13; B: 9, 15, 12; C: 10, 10, 10. Which team's readings are most consistent?
options: Team A, because its average is highest
Team C, because its readings show no spread
Team B, because its values are different
All teams, because each has three readings
questions.explanation: Consistency is about how close repeated readings are to one another. Team C recorded the same value each time.
questions.difficultyRationale: The answer requires comparing variation across three sets rather than selecting the largest value.

questions.question: A student grows two seedlings but gives one more light and more water. It grows taller. What can the student conclude from this test?
options: More light alone caused the extra growth
More water alone caused the extra growth
The combined conditions were associated with greater growth, but the separate effects are unknown
Light and water have no effect
questions.explanation: Because light and water changed together, their individual effects cannot be separated. A fair follow-up changes one factor at a time.
questions.difficultyRationale: It evaluates a confounded experiment and identifies what the evidence can and cannot establish.

questions.question: A group claims that every shiny object is a metal after testing a coin and a steel spoon. Which follow-up best checks the claim?
options: Polish the spoon until it shines more
Test a wider range of shiny and non-shiny materials using more than appearance
questions.explanation: A conclusion about all materials needs a broader sample and properties beyond appearance; shine alone does not prove that something is a metal.
questions.difficultyRationale: It challenges overgeneralisation and requires choosing a broader evidence-based test.

questions.question: A model uses a small ball for Earth and a lamp for the Sun. Which conclusion cannot be made reliably from this model if the spacing is not to scale?
options: The actual distance between Earth and the Sun
That light from the lamp can illuminate one side of the ball
That a sphere can represent Earth
That turning the ball changes the lit side
questions.explanation: A model can demonstrate illumination and rotation, but unscaled spacing cannot show the real Earth–Sun distance.
questions.difficultyRationale: The learner must distinguish what a model represents from what it cannot represent.

questions.question: A student records that a metal spoon feels cooler than a wooden spoon in the same room. Which statement is an observation rather than an explanation?
options: The metal must contain more cold
The spoon feels cooler when touched
Metal always has a lower temperature
questions.explanation: The feeling is the direct observation. Claims about the materials' temperatures or heat production need separate evidence.
questions.difficultyRationale: It separates observed evidence from competing explanations.

questions.question: A ruler is used to measure a pencil, but the pencil begins at the 2 cm mark and ends at 14 cm. What length should be recorded, and why?
options: 14 cm, because the end mark is the length
16 cm, because both marks are added
12 cm, because the starting reading must be subtracted
2 cm, because that is where measurement began
questions.explanation: The length is 14 − 2 = 12 cm. A measurement is the difference between the end and start readings.
questions.difficultyRationale: It combines reading two scale positions with the correct measurement operation.

questions.question: A student tests a claim using one trial and gets an unexpected result. Which next step gives the strongest evidence?
options: Discard the result without recording it
Ask another student to guess the answer
Repeat the same controlled procedure, record all readings and compare the pattern
questions.explanation: Repeating a controlled test helps show whether the unusual result is reproducible and whether a procedural error occurred.
questions.difficultyRationale: It requires selecting a verification strategy rather than reacting to one result.

questions.question: Which nutrient is the body's main quick source of energy?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are a major energy-giving nutrient.

questions.question: Which food is a good source of protein?
questions.explanation: Pulses such as lentils provide protein.

questions.question: Which mineral is important for strong bones and teeth?
questions.explanation: Calcium supports bone and teeth health.

questions.question: Which solution is commonly used to test food for starch?
questions.explanation: Iodine turns blue-black when starch is present.

questions.question: Which vitamin deficiency can cause night blindness?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is needed for normal vision in dim light.

questions.question: Which food is especially rich in fats?
questions.explanation: Butter contains a high proportion of fat.

questions.question: Why does the body need protein?
options: For growth and repair of body tissues
questions.explanation: Proteins help build and repair tissues.

questions.question: Which meal combination supplies both carbohydrates and protein?
questions.explanation: Rice supplies carbohydrates and dal supplies protein.

questions.question: Which vitamin deficiency causes scurvy?
questions.explanation: Scurvy results from inadequate vitamin C.

questions.question: What is the main role of dietary fibre?
options: It helps food move through the digestive tract
questions.explanation: Fibre supports bowel movement.

questions.question: Which mineral is needed to make haemoglobin?
questions.explanation: Iron is a component of haemoglobin.

questions.question: A diet based almost entirely on polished rice may lack enough of which nutrient if pulses are absent?
questions.explanation: Rice is mainly carbohydrate; pulses are an important protein source.

questions.question: Which is the most balanced meal?
options: Chapati, dal, vegetables, curd and fruit
questions.explanation: It combines several nutrient groups and fibre.

questions.question: Why is water an essential component of food?
options: It helps transport substances and regulate body temperature
It is needed only during exercise
questions.explanation: Water supports transport and temperature regulation.

questions.question: Which pair is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D helps the body use calcium and supports bones.

questions.question: A food sample turns blue-black after iodine is added. What is present?
questions.explanation: Blue-black is the positive iodine test for starch.

questions.question: A child has bleeding gums after eating very few fruits and vegetables. Which deficiency is likely?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C deficiency can cause scurvy and bleeding gums.

questions.question: Which pair is a useful plant-based protein combination?
questions.explanation: Beans supply protein and cereals complement their amino-acid profile.

questions.question: Why should people eat different kinds of food?
options: Every food contains all nutrients equally
questions.explanation: A varied diet helps meet nutritional needs.

questions.question: Which food mainly adds roughage to a meal?
questions.explanation: Fruit pulp and skin supply dietary fibre.

questions.question: Which foods can help improve iron intake?
questions.explanation: Beans and leafy greens can provide iron.

questions.question: Which statement about fats is correct?
options: They have no role in the body
They provide energy and help absorb some vitamins
They are the only nutrient needed for growth
questions.explanation: Fats supply energy and help absorb vitamins A, D, E and K.

questions.question: A child's balanced diet should consider:
questions.explanation: Nutritional needs vary with growth and activity.

questions.question: Why is iodised salt useful?
options: It helps prevent iodine-deficiency disorders such as goitre
questions.explanation: Iodine is needed for thyroid hormone production.

questions.question: Which vitamin can the skin make with suitable sunlight exposure?
questions.explanation: Sunlight enables vitamin D production in skin.

questions.question: A person gets enough calories but too few vitamins and minerals. What can happen?
options: The body no longer needs water
questions.explanation: Energy alone does not ensure adequate micronutrients.

questions.question: Which is a protective-food choice?
questions.explanation: Fruits and vegetables provide vitamins and minerals.

questions.question: Why should excess salt intake be avoided?
options: Too much sodium can contribute to high blood pressure
questions.explanation: High sodium intake is associated with raised blood pressure.

questions.question: Which nutrient is abundant in milk and curd and supports bones?
questions.explanation: Milk products are common calcium sources.

questions.question: Removing bran from whole grains reduces which food component most?
questions.explanation: Bran is a fibre-rich outer layer of grains.

questions.question: Which deficiency can cause rickets in children?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D deficiency can impair bone mineralisation.

questions.question: Which pair contains only energy-yielding nutrients?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates and fats provide energy.

questions.question: A meal has rice, vegetables, dal and oil but no fruit. Which addition best improves vitamin C intake?
questions.explanation: Guava is rich in vitamin C.

questions.question: Why include green leafy vegetables regularly?
options: They provide fibre, vitamins and minerals
questions.explanation: Leafy vegetables contribute several micronutrients.

questions.question: Which food is likely to provide the most protein per usual serving?
questions.explanation: Chickpeas are pulses and provide protein.

questions.question: An enlarged thyroid caused by iodine deficiency is commonly called:
questions.explanation: Iodine deficiency can cause thyroid enlargement.

questions.question: Why are vitamins needed even in small amounts?
options: They help regulate important body processes
questions.explanation: Vitamins support normal growth and body functions.

questions.question: Which breakfast is likely to provide more fibre?
questions.explanation: Whole grains and fruit provide fibre.

questions.question: A food label lists 18 g sugar per serving. How much sugar is in two servings?
Why may an active teenager need more energy than a less active child of similar age?
options: Exercise removes the need for protein
Active muscles do not need water
More energy is used during physical activity
questions.explanation: Physical activity increases energy use.

questions.question: Two meals provide equal energy. One includes vegetables, pulses and fruit; the other is mostly sweets. Which is better for everyday nutrition?
options: The meal made mostly of sweets
The meal with vegetables, pulses and fruit
questions.explanation: The varied meal provides more kinds of nutrients and fibre.

questions.question: Which sample is most likely to turn blue-black with iodine?
questions.explanation: Bread contains starch.

questions.question: A snack contains 30 g carbohydrate, 10 g protein and 5 g fat. Using 4 kcal/g for carbohydrate and protein and 9 kcal/g for fat, how much energy does it provide?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrate: 30×4=120 kcal; protein: 10×4=40 kcal; fat: 5×9=45 kcal. Total = 205 kcal.
questions.difficultyRationale: It requires three separate energy calculations followed by addition.

questions.question: Two lunch boxes provide the same energy. Box A has 8 g protein and Box B has 14 g protein. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Box A must be healthier in every way
Box B provides more protein, but the full balance of nutrients still needs to be compared
Both boxes contain equal protein because their energy is equal
questions.explanation: Equal energy does not mean equal nutrient content. Box B has more protein, but a balanced-diet judgement also considers other nutrients and food groups.
questions.difficultyRationale: It distinguishes energy content from nutrient balance and avoids an unsupported overall health claim.

questions.question: A child eats mostly rice and sweets and very little dal, beans or other protein-rich food. Which change most directly improves the missing part of the diet?
options: Add pulses, beans or another suitable protein-rich food while keeping the meal varied
questions.explanation: Pulses and beans add protein. A varied meal should still include other food groups rather than replacing them all.
questions.difficultyRationale: It links a dietary pattern to a nutrient need and selects a targeted correction.

questions.question: A food label says a serving is 25 g and contains 12 g protein per 100 g. How much protein is in one serving?
questions.explanation: A 25 g serving is one-quarter of 100 g, so protein = 12÷4 = 3 g.
questions.difficultyRationale: It requires interpreting a per-100-g label and scaling to the actual serving.

questions.question: A child has difficulty seeing in dim light. Which food choice most directly helps supply the nutrient associated with normal vision?
options: Carrot and leafy vegetables that provide vitamin A precursors
questions.explanation: Carrots and many leafy vegetables contain carotenoids that the body can use to make vitamin A, which supports normal vision.
questions.difficultyRationale: It connects a symptom clue with a nutrient function and suitable food sources.

questions.question: A meal has enough energy but very little dietary fibre. Which addition best addresses that gap without simply adding more sugar?
options: A serving of vegetables, fruit or whole grains
questions.explanation: Vegetables, fruit and whole grains can add dietary fibre. Fibre supports healthy digestion, while sugary drinks do not solve the gap.
questions.difficultyRationale: It asks the learner to identify a nutrient gap and choose a food group that addresses it.

questions.question: A student compares two breakfasts: P has 6 g protein and 4 g fibre; Q has 9 g protein and 1 g fibre. Which statement is accurate?
options: P has more protein and fibre
Q has more fibre but less protein
Q has more protein, while P has more fibre
Both have the same amounts of both
questions.explanation: Compare each nutrient separately: Q has 9 g protein versus 6 g, while P has 4 g fibre versus 1 g.
questions.difficultyRationale: It requires comparing two independent measures and resisting a single overall ranking.

questions.question: A family wants a varied meal using rice, lentils, vegetables and curd. Which explanation best describes why this is a stronger plan than eating only rice?
options: Rice alone supplies every nutrient in the right amount
Curd and lentils should replace all other foods
The foods contribute different nutrients, so the combination is more varied and balanced
questions.explanation: Different foods contribute different nutrients. Combining grains, pulses, vegetables and dairy can improve variety and balance.
questions.difficultyRationale: It integrates the functions of several food groups to evaluate a whole meal.

questions.question: Which material is transparent?
questions.explanation: Transparent materials allow most light to pass through clearly.

questions.question: Which property makes rubber useful for elastic bands?
options: It can stretch and return towards its original shape
questions.explanation: Rubber is elastic.

questions.question: Which object is made from a good electrical conductor?
questions.explanation: Copper allows electric current to pass through readily.

questions.question: Which material is generally opaque?
options: Clear water in a thin layer
questions.explanation: Wood does not allow light to pass through.

questions.question: Which material is attracted strongly by a magnet?
questions.explanation: Iron is magnetic.

questions.question: A material that allows some light through but not a clear image is:
questions.explanation: Translucent materials scatter light.

questions.question: Which property makes cotton useful for towels?
questions.explanation: Cotton fibres absorb water.

questions.question: Which item is suitable for a window because it is transparent and rigid?
questions.explanation: Glass is rigid and allows light through.

questions.question: Why is aluminium often used to make cooking vessels?
options: It is a poor heat conductor
It conducts heat and is relatively light
questions.explanation: Aluminium transfers heat well and is lightweight.

questions.question: Which object is most likely to float on water?
questions.explanation: Wood is generally less dense than water.

questions.question: A sponge changes shape when squeezed and partly regains it after release. Which property is shown?
questions.explanation: The sponge deforms and partly returns to its shape.

questions.question: Which pair consists of good thermal insulators?
questions.explanation: Wood and many plastics transfer heat slowly.

questions.question: A material breaks easily when hit and does not bend first. It is:
questions.explanation: Brittle materials fracture with little bending.

questions.question: Which material is used to cover electrical wires?
questions.explanation: Plastic is an electrical insulator.

questions.question: Which observation shows a material is soluble in water?
options: It remains as large pieces at the bottom
It forms a uniform solution when stirred
It is attracted to a magnet
questions.explanation: A soluble substance forms a uniform mixture.

questions.question: Sand is stirred into water and left undisturbed. What happens?
questions.explanation: Sand is insoluble and settles under gravity.

questions.question: Which substance is both hard and transparent?
questions.explanation: Glass is hard and can transmit light clearly.

questions.question: A steel spoon feels colder than a wooden spoon in the same room. Why?
options: Steel is always below room temperature
Steel transfers heat from the hand faster
The spoon's mass changes its temperature
questions.explanation: Steel is a better thermal conductor than wood.

questions.question: A raincoat material should be:
questions.explanation: A raincoat should prevent water passing through.

questions.question: A container should show the water level without opening it. Which property is useful?
questions.explanation: A transparent container lets the water level be seen.

questions.question: A wax piece floats in water. What can be inferred?
options: Its average density is less than water
questions.explanation: Objects less dense than water generally float.

questions.question: Which material is suitable for a hot pan handle?
questions.explanation: Wood is a poor heat conductor.

questions.question: Which non-metal can conduct electricity and is used in some electrodes?
questions.explanation: Graphite is a form of carbon that conducts electricity, even though it is a non-metal.

questions.question: Why are pan bodies often metal but handles wood or plastic?
options: Metal conducts heat; wood and plastic insulate
Metal is transparent; wood is magnetic
questions.explanation: The vessel transfers heat while the handle reduces heat transfer to the hand.

questions.question: Which material is most likely translucent?
questions.explanation: Frosted glass passes light but blurs objects behind it.

questions.question: A student compares four powders for solubility. Which method is fair?
options: Use different amounts of each powder
Use equal masses, equal water volumes and equal stirring time
questions.explanation: Keep conditions controlled to compare dissolving fairly.

questions.question: Which object is made from a ductile material?
questions.explanation: Ductile materials can be drawn into wires.

questions.question: A material can be hammered into thin sheets. It shows:
questions.explanation: Malleable materials can be shaped into sheets.

questions.question: A plastic bottle stores water because plastic is generally:
options: Light, waterproof and does not rust
questions.explanation: Common plastics are lightweight and water-resistant.

questions.question: An object floats in water but sinks in cooking oil. What does this tell us?
options: Its density is less than water but greater than the oil
questions.explanation: Cooking oil is generally less dense than water; the object's density lies between the two liquids, so it floats in water but sinks in oil.

questions.question: A material is not attracted to a magnet. Which conclusion is safest?
options: It is not attracted to this magnet in this test
questions.explanation: A negative magnet test does not prove absence of all metals.

questions.question: Why can a metal spoon's handle become hot when left in hot soup?
questions.explanation: Metals conduct heat along their length.

questions.question: Choose the accurate association between a material and one of its properties.
questions.explanation: Rubber can stretch and return towards its shape.

questions.question: Which fabric absorbs water and allows air to pass through?
questions.explanation: Cotton is absorbent and breathable.

questions.question: A sharp image forms through a sheet onto a screen. What does this suggest?
options: The sheet transmits light with little scattering
questions.explanation: A clear image requires light to pass with little scattering.

questions.question: How should absorbency of two cloth samples be compared?
options: Measure water absorbed under the same conditions
questions.explanation: Water uptake is measured consistently.

questions.question: A material is stiff, strong and corrosion-resistant. A suitable use is:
questions.explanation: Steel is strong; treatment helps limit corrosion.

questions.question: Why is a glass tumbler unsuitable as a hammer?
options: Glass is brittle and can shatter on impact
questions.explanation: Brittle materials can break under sudden impact.

questions.question: Two equal-size blocks have different masses. Which statement is correct?
options: The heavier block has greater density
The lighter block has greater volume
questions.explanation: At equal volume, greater mass means greater density.

questions.question: An object floats partly above water. What happens if it is pushed fully under and released?
options: It tends to rise towards the surface
questions.explanation: Upthrust exceeds its weight until it rises.

questions.question: A transparent liquid looks clear. Does that prove it is safe to drink?
options: Yes, all clear liquids are safe
Yes, if it has no colour
No, every transparent liquid is poisonous
No; appearance alone cannot establish safety
questions.explanation: Harmful substances can be colourless.

questions.question: Which combination is best for an umbrella canopy?
questions.explanation: The canopy should repel water while remaining light and flexible.

questions.question: A school needs a cover that lets light through, bends without breaking easily and does not soak up rain. Which material best fits all three needs?
options: A thick piece of blotting paper
questions.explanation: A suitable plastic sheet can be transparent, flexible and water-resistant; the other choices fail at least one required property.
questions.difficultyRationale: It combines three material properties and selects the only option that satisfies all constraints.

questions.question: A mixture contains iron pins, sand and small plastic pieces. Which sequence separates all three most sensibly?
options: Use a magnet to remove iron, then sort the plastic from the sand
Add water and evaporate it before using a magnet
Heat the mixture until the plastic disappears
questions.explanation: A magnet removes the iron. The remaining plastic pieces can be picked out or separated by a suitable size-based method, leaving sand.
questions.difficultyRationale: It plans a sequence using two different physical properties without changing the materials chemically.

questions.question: Four samples are tested. P is transparent and waterproof; Q is opaque and magnetic; R is translucent and absorbent; S is transparent but dissolves in water. Which sample is most suitable for a clear rain shield?
questions.explanation: A rain shield should let light through and resist water. P is the only sample with both properties.
questions.difficultyRationale: It uses a set of test results to match a material to two functional requirements.

questions.question: A same-sized wooden block floats while a metal block sinks in water. Which explanation is best?
options: The wooden block is always heavier
Water pushes only wooden objects upward
For these blocks, the wood is less dense than water while the metal is denser
The metal block has no volume
questions.explanation: Floating and sinking depend on average density relative to the liquid, not simply on whether an object looks large or small.
questions.difficultyRationale: It compares material behaviour and applies the idea of floating and sinking to explain the result.

questions.question: A student says a material is soluble because it disappears when stirred into water. Which extra check is best before concluding it has dissolved?
options: Filter the mixture and see whether solid remains, then gently evaporate a small sample to check for residue
Stir it faster and assume it is soluble
Look only at the colour of the container
Add more of the same material until the water is full
questions.explanation: Filtering checks for undissolved particles; evaporation can show whether the material was present in the water as a dissolved substance.
questions.difficultyRationale: It distinguishes dissolving from merely breaking into particles suspended in water.

questions.question: A window must be made from a material that allows a clear view and does not absorb rain. Which pair of tests is most relevant?
options: Check whether it is magnetic and rough
Check whether it is heavy and coloured
Check whether it can be crushed by hand
questions.explanation: Transparency determines whether a clear view is possible, and water absorption helps assess its suitability for exposure to rain.
questions.difficultyRationale: It chooses the two tests that directly match the intended use.

questions.question: A wire has a metal core and a rubber covering. Which explanation best accounts for using two different materials?
options: Both materials are used because they are equally magnetic
Rubber carries the electric current better than metal
The metal core conducts electricity while the rubber covering helps insulate the outside
The rubber makes the metal dissolve
questions.explanation: Metals such as copper conduct electricity; rubber is an electrical insulator and helps protect people from contact with the conducting core.
questions.difficultyRationale: It integrates the distinct properties of two materials and their roles in one object.

questions.question: Two cloth samples are compared for making a towel. Sample A absorbs 18 mL of water in the test and Sample B absorbs 11 mL. Which conclusion is justified if equal-sized pieces were tested in the same way?
options: The test proves A will dry faster
A absorbed more water under the test conditions, but drying speed needs a separate test
questions.explanation: The test measures absorption, not drying rate. A absorbed 7 mL more, but drying depends on other conditions too.
questions.difficultyRationale: It requires careful interpretation of what a property test measures and what it does not.

title: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: In which state does water have a fixed shape?
questions.explanation: A solid has a fixed shape.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: What is the change from liquid water to ice called?
questions.explanation: Freezing changes liquid water into solid ice.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: What is the change from ice to liquid water called?
questions.explanation: Melting occurs when solid ice gains heat.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Which process changes liquid water into water vapour at the surface?
questions.explanation: Evaporation happens at the surface of a liquid.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Which process forms liquid droplets when water vapour cools?
questions.explanation: Cooling water vapour can turn it into liquid droplets.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Why does a wet shirt dry faster on a warm, windy day?
options: Warmth and moving air increase evaporation
questions.explanation: Higher temperature and moving air usually speed evaporation.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Where does water vapour in the air come from?
options: Evaporation from water and transpiration from plants
questions.explanation: Water enters the air through evaporation and plant transpiration.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: What is dew?
options: Water droplets formed on cool surfaces by condensation
questions.explanation: Water vapour condenses on surfaces that have cooled.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Which statement about evaporation is correct?
options: It can occur at temperatures below the boiling point
It happens only inside a liquid
It changes water directly into ice
questions.explanation: Evaporation can occur from a liquid surface at many temperatures.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: What happens to water in an open dish left in sunlight for several hours?
options: Some water evaporates into the air
questions.explanation: Liquid water changes into water vapour.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Why does water kept in an earthen pot often become cooler?
options: Some water evaporates through tiny pores and takes heat away
The pot blocks all heat transfer
questions.explanation: Evaporation removes heat from the pot and remaining water.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Which factor usually increases the rate of evaporation?
questions.explanation: A larger surface lets more liquid particles escape.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Why does water boil faster in a covered pot than in an open pot?
options: The cover reduces heat loss and helps the water heat efficiently
The cover lowers the boiling point to zero
The cover removes water vapour permanently
The cover turns water into ice
questions.explanation: A lid reduces heat loss to the surroundings.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: At normal atmospheric pressure, pure water boils at about:
questions.explanation: At standard atmospheric pressure, water's boiling point is about 100°C.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: At normal atmospheric pressure, pure water freezes at about:
questions.explanation: The freezing point of pure water is about 0°C.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: A cold glass is taken from a refrigerator and droplets appear outside it. Where do the droplets come from?
options: Water vapour in the surrounding air
Water formed from the glass material
Ice melting inside the glass only
questions.explanation: Air near the cold surface cools and water vapour condenses.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Why can puddles disappear even when the Sun is not shining directly on them?
options: Evaporation can occur without direct sunlight
Water can only vanish by boiling
questions.explanation: Evaporation occurs at ordinary temperatures.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Which stage of the water cycle returns water from clouds to Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: Rain, snow and hail are forms of precipitation.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: What is the main energy source that drives evaporation in the water cycle?
questions.explanation: Solar energy warms water and supports evaporation.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Why do tiny water droplets form on the outside of a bottle filled with ice-cold water?
options: The bottle leaks through solid glass
Water vapour in air condenses on the cold bottle
The ice passes through the bottle wall
questions.explanation: The cold surface cools nearby air and causes condensation.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Which change of state takes place when steam forms above boiling water?
questions.explanation: Boiling converts liquid water into water vapour.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: What is the difference between boiling and evaporation?
options: Boiling occurs only at the surface
They are exactly the same process
Boiling occurs throughout the liquid; evaporation occurs at the surface
questions.explanation: Boiling forms vapour throughout the liquid; evaporation is a surface process.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Why does evaporation cause cooling?
options: The liquid gains heat from the air
Higher-energy particles escape, lowering the average energy of the remaining liquid
questions.explanation: Escaping particles carry energy away from the liquid.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Why does a fan help wet skin feel cooler?
options: The fan lowers body temperature by making ice
Moving air speeds evaporation of sweat
The fan stops sweat from evaporating
questions.explanation: Air movement increases evaporation, which removes heat.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: A wet floor dries faster when spread into a thin layer than when left in a small puddle. Why?
options: The thin layer has a larger exposed surface area
The thin layer has more water
questions.explanation: A larger surface area increases evaporation.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Which description best fits a cloud?
options: A solid mass of water vapour
A layer of liquid water floating above Earth
A collection of tiny water droplets or ice crystals in the air
questions.explanation: Clouds contain tiny liquid droplets and/or ice crystals.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Fog forms when:
options: Water vapour condenses into tiny droplets near the ground
questions.explanation: Fog is a cloud at or near the ground.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Why can droplets form on grass early in the morning?
options: The grass releases liquid water from its roots onto every blade
The grass cools and water vapour condenses on it
The Sun turns soil into water
questions.explanation: Cool surfaces can collect dew through condensation.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: A puddle shrinks from 2 cm depth to 1 cm depth in warm air. Which process best explains the change?
questions.explanation: Liquid water enters the air as vapour.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: What happens to the temperature of pure water while it is boiling steadily at normal pressure?
options: It rises continuously above 100°C while boiling
It remains about 100°C until the liquid has boiled away
questions.explanation: At a fixed pressure, energy supplied during boiling is used for the change of state.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Which condition would make a wet cloth dry most slowly?
questions.explanation: Low temperature, low airflow and high humidity slow evaporation.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Why does water vapour rise and later form clouds at cooler heights?
options: Rising moist air expands and cools, allowing condensation
Air pressure turns water into salt
Clouds are made by sunlight alone
questions.explanation: Cooling moist air can reach saturation and form droplets.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: A student puts equal amounts of water into two plates. One plate is wide and the other narrow. Which should lose water faster under the same conditions?
options: Both must evaporate at exactly the same rate
questions.explanation: The wide plate exposes a larger surface area.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Why is the water cycle called a cycle?
options: Water is created whenever it rains
Water moves repeatedly between Earth's surface and the atmosphere
questions.explanation: Evaporation, condensation and precipitation continually move water.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Which process changes water vapour directly into ice crystals?
questions.explanation: Deposition is a gas-to-solid change, such as frost formation.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Frost forms on a very cold surface when:
options: Water vapour changes directly into ice
questions.explanation: Frost can form by deposition of water vapour.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Why does a puddle evaporate more slowly on a humid day?
options: The air already contains a lot of water vapour
Humidity removes all heat from the puddle
Humidity turns the puddle into ice
questions.explanation: High humidity reduces the rate at which more water vapour enters the air.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: A student places a wet paper strip near a fan and another in still air. Which result is expected?
options: The strip in still air always dries first
The strip near the fan dries faster
questions.explanation: Moving air carries water vapour away from the surface.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Why does a mirror become misty after a person takes a hot shower?
options: Warm moist air condenses on the cooler mirror
The shower changes glass into liquid
questions.explanation: Water vapour cools at the mirror and forms droplets.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: A sealed bottle of water is warmed gently. Why does its total mass remain the same if no water escapes?
options: A change of state does not remove water from the sealed system
questions.explanation: The water is redistributed between liquid and vapour but remains in the system.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: A wet cloth is hung in a room at 25°C. Which change would usually make it dry faster?
options: Fold it into a thick bundle
Place it in a closed humid cupboard
questions.explanation: Moving air removes water vapour from near the cloth.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Why is the cooling effect of evaporation useful in sweating?
options: Evaporation of sweat removes heat from the skin
questions.explanation: Evaporation takes energy from the skin surface.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water

questions.question: Two equal wet cloths are placed in the same room. One is spread out and the other is folded. Why is the spread cloth expected to dry sooner?
options: More of its surface is exposed to air, allowing faster evaporation
Its water changes into ice first
The spread cloth has less water by definition
questions.explanation: Spreading increases the exposed surface area, so more water can evaporate at a time when other conditions are similar.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water
questions.difficultyRationale: It links surface area to evaporation while controlling the comparison.

questions.question: A cold bottle is taken from a refrigerator into a warm room. Drops form on the outside, although the bottle is sealed. Where does this water come from?
options: Water leaking through the bottle wall
Water vapour in the surrounding air cooling and condensing
Ice inside the bottle passing through the cap
questions.explanation: Water vapour in the air touches the cold surface, cools and condenses into liquid droplets. A sealed bottle need not leak.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water
questions.difficultyRationale: It follows the source of water through a change of state and rules out a tempting alternative.

questions.question: A student tests evaporation using equal amounts of water in a wide plate and a narrow glass. The plate loses water faster. What is the strongest conclusion?
options: The larger exposed surface may explain the faster loss, provided other conditions were alike
The water in the glass has changed into a solid
questions.explanation: A wider exposed surface allows more water molecules to escape into the air. The conclusion is valid only if temperature, airflow and other conditions were comparable.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water
questions.difficultyRationale: It interprets an experiment and checks the conditions needed for a fair conclusion.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes water moving from a pond into clouds and later returning as rain?
options: Evaporation, condensation, cloud droplets grow, precipitation
questions.explanation: Water evaporates from the pond, vapour cools and condenses into droplets, droplets combine and eventually fall as precipitation.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water
questions.difficultyRationale: It requires ordering several linked stages of the water cycle.

questions.question: Grass is wet early in the morning although it did not rain overnight. The air cooled during the night. Which explanation best fits the evidence?
options: Water vapour in the air condensed on the cool grass
Water travelled up from the soil through the sky
The Sun melted ice on every blade
questions.explanation: As the grass cooled, nearby water vapour condensed on its surface, forming dew.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water
questions.difficultyRationale: It applies condensation to a real situation and distinguishes dew from rainfall.

questions.question: A sealed clear jar contains a little water and is placed in sunlight. Water droplets later appear on the inside wall above the water. Which sequence explains the droplets?
options: The jar makes water from sunlight
Some liquid evaporates, vapour touches a cooler wall and condenses
The water passes through the glass as a liquid
The droplets are dust that has melted
questions.explanation: Water evaporates from the liquid, then vapour cools at the inner wall and condenses into droplets. The jar allows the cycle to be observed.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water
questions.difficultyRationale: It tracks two state changes in the correct order within one model.

questions.question: A pot of water is heated. Small bubbles appear at the bottom before the whole liquid boils. Which observation would best distinguish boiling from ordinary surface evaporation?
options: Only the water surface loses particles
Bubbles form throughout the liquid as it reaches its boiling condition
The water changes directly into ice
questions.explanation: Evaporation can occur at the surface at many temperatures; boiling involves bubbles forming throughout the liquid.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water
questions.difficultyRationale: It compares two similar processes and identifies the decisive observation.

questions.question: Two equal bowls of water are kept side by side. Bowl A is near a fan and Bowl B is in still air. A loses more water. What additional check would make the inference about airflow stronger?
options: Use different bowl sizes as well
Add salt to Bowl A only
Measure the bowls with different rulers
Repeat with equal bowls, equal water and the same temperature while changing only airflow
questions.explanation: Repeating with all other conditions held alike tests whether airflow is responsible for the difference in evaporation.
questions.syllabusTopic: A Journey through States of Water
questions.difficultyRationale: It designs a controlled follow-up to isolate one factor.

questions.question: Which method separates stones from rice when the stones are visible and large?
questions.explanation: Handpicking removes visible unwanted particles.

questions.question: Which method separates husk from heavier grains using moving air?
questions.explanation: Lighter husk is carried away while grains fall.

questions.question: How should sand be separated from water?
questions.explanation: Sand settles; clearer water is poured off.

questions.question: Which method removes tea leaves from brewed tea?
questions.explanation: A strainer lets liquid through and retains leaves.

questions.question: Which process obtains salt from seawater?
questions.explanation: Water evaporates, leaving salt.

questions.question: A mixture contains iron filings and sand. Which tool is useful?
questions.explanation: Iron is attracted to a magnet.

questions.question: Which method separates flour from larger bran particles?
questions.explanation: Flour passes through mesh; larger particles remain.

questions.question: Which process loosens grains from harvested stalks?
questions.explanation: Threshing separates grain from stalks.

questions.question: Why is filter paper used in filtration?
options: Its pores let liquid pass but retain insoluble solids
questions.explanation: Filter paper retains suspended insoluble particles.

questions.question: Which method separates butter from curd?
questions.explanation: Churning helps butter separate from curd.

questions.question: A mixture has pebbles, sand and water. Which sequence is sensible?
options: Use a magnet for all three
Remove pebbles by sieving, then filter sand from water
questions.explanation: Sieving removes pebbles; filtration separates sand from water.

questions.question: Why is sedimentation useful before decantation?
options: It lets heavier insoluble particles settle
questions.explanation: Settling makes the upper liquid clearer.

questions.question: Salt and sand are stirred into water. Which sequence separates both?
options: Filter out sand, then evaporate the filtrate
questions.explanation: Sand is filtered; dissolved salt is recovered by evaporation.

questions.question: Which mixture is best separated by a sieve?
questions.explanation: Different particle sizes allow sieving.

questions.question: Which method depends mainly on particle size?
questions.explanation: Sieving separates particles by mesh size.

questions.question: Alum is added to muddy water before standing. Why?
options: It helps fine suspended particles clump and settle
questions.explanation: Alum assists fine particles to form heavier clumps.

questions.question: A student filters muddy water. What remains on the paper?
questions.explanation: Filter paper retains insoluble particles.

questions.question: How can oil and water be separated in a simple classroom set-up?
options: Let layers form, then carefully decant one layer
questions.explanation: Oil and water are immiscible and form layers.

questions.question: Why cannot ordinary filtration remove dissolved salt from water?
options: Salt passes through the filter with the water
questions.explanation: Dissolved particles travel with the liquid.

questions.question: What condition helps winnowing?
options: Still air in a closed room
A steady breeze or moving air
questions.explanation: Moving air carries away lighter husk.

questions.question: A mixture has metal pins and rice grains. Which property enables separation?
options: The pins are attracted by a magnet
questions.explanation: Magnetic pins can be removed from rice.

questions.question: Fine clay remains suspended in muddy water. What can be added to help it settle?
questions.explanation: Alum helps fine suspended particles clump and settle.

questions.question: Which process should be done before winnowing harvested grain?
questions.explanation: Threshing loosens grains first.

questions.question: In filtration, the liquid that passes through the filter is called:
questions.explanation: The collected liquid is the filtrate.

questions.question: In filtration, the solid left on the filter paper is called:
questions.explanation: The retained solid is the residue.

questions.question: A mixture contains salt, sand and iron filings. What is the best first step?
options: Use a magnet to remove iron filings
questions.explanation: A magnet removes iron without affecting salt or sand.

questions.question: After removing iron from salt-sand mixture, how can the remaining solids be separated?
options: Dissolve salt in water, filter sand, then evaporate
questions.explanation: Salt dissolves; sand does not. Filter and evaporate.

questions.question: Why does decantation work after sedimentation?
options: The settled solid stays behind while clearer liquid is poured off
questions.explanation: Careful pouring separates the upper liquid from settled particles.

questions.question: How can mixed pulses of different sizes be sorted?
questions.explanation: Mesh sizes separate particles by size.

questions.question: Which methods are used in traditional wheat processing?
questions.explanation: Threshing loosens grains; winnowing removes lighter chaff.

questions.question: A student filters sugar dissolved in water. What passes through?
questions.explanation: Dissolved sugar passes through with water.

questions.question: Why can evaporation recover a dissolved solid?
options: The solvent turns into a filter
The solvent becomes vapour while the solid remains
The solid becomes lighter than air
questions.explanation: Evaporation removes solvent and leaves dissolved material.

questions.question: Chalk powder is mixed with water and filtered. What is collected below?
options: Water with most chalk retained on the paper
questions.explanation: Insoluble chalk is held back; water passes through.

questions.question: What is the main use of a funnel during filtration?
options: It guides the mixture into the filter without spilling
questions.explanation: The funnel supports the filter and directs liquid.

questions.question: Which method can recover both water and salt from salt water?
questions.explanation: Distillation evaporates water and condenses it for collection.

questions.question: During distillation of salt water, what is collected in the receiver?
questions.explanation: Water vapour cools and condenses into liquid.

questions.question: Which mixture cannot be separated by ordinary filtration alone?
questions.explanation: Dissolved sugar passes through with water.

questions.question: Why pour slowly along a glass rod during decantation?
options: To reduce disturbance of the settled sediment
questions.explanation: A guided pour helps keep settled particles behind.

questions.question: Salt and sawdust are mixed with water. What is likely?
questions.explanation: Salt is soluble; sawdust is insoluble and usually less dense.

questions.question: How can salt be recovered from salt water containing sawdust?
options: Remove sawdust, then evaporate the salt solution
questions.explanation: Remove sawdust, then evaporate water to leave salt.

questions.question: Which method mainly uses magnetic properties?
questions.explanation: A magnet attracts selected magnetic materials.

questions.question: Why can winnowing separate chaff from grain?
options: Lighter chaff is carried farther by moving air
Grains dissolve while chaff does not
questions.explanation: The method uses differences in how air carries particles.

questions.question: A dry mixture contains iron filings, sand and salt. Which sequence can recover each component without mixing them again?
options: Use a magnet for iron, dissolve the salt in water, filter out sand, then evaporate the water
Evaporate first, then use a magnet on the vapour
Filter the dry mixture, then pour away the salt
Use winnowing to remove the dissolved salt
questions.explanation: A magnet removes iron. Water dissolves salt but not sand; filtration collects sand, and evaporation recovers salt.
questions.difficultyRationale: It combines magnetic separation, dissolving, filtration and evaporation in a purposeful order.

questions.question: A farmer wants to separate light husk from heavier grains after threshing. Which method works best and why?
options: Sieving, because both have exactly the same size
Winnowing, because moving air carries the lighter husk farther
Filtration, because grains dissolve in water
questions.explanation: Winnowing uses air to carry the lighter husk away while heavier grains fall nearby.
questions.difficultyRationale: It matches a method to a difference in mass and predicts how both materials behave.

questions.question: A jar contains sand, water and a layer of cooking oil. Which first action best separates the oil from the other two materials?
options: Filter the whole mixture through cloth
Allow the layers to settle, then carefully decant the top oil layer
Use a magnet to pull out the oil
questions.explanation: Oil forms a separate upper layer above water. Letting the mixture settle and carefully decanting separates the oil before dealing with the sand.
questions.difficultyRationale: It uses settling and density-related layering to choose the first step in a multi-part separation.

questions.question: Salt dissolved in clear water passes through ordinary filter paper. What does this show?
options: The salt has turned into water
Dissolved salt particles travel with the water through the filter
questions.explanation: Filtration removes insoluble particles, not a substance dissolved in the liquid. Evaporation is needed to recover the salt.
questions.difficultyRationale: It distinguishes a solution from a suspension and selects the correct next process.

questions.question: A cup of sweet tea contains dissolved sugar and loose tea leaves. Which order gives tea without leaves and can later recover sugar from the liquid?
options: Filter the tea leaves first, then evaporate the liquid if sugar must be recovered
Evaporate the cup before removing the leaves
Use a magnet to collect the sugar
Use a sieve to remove dissolved sugar
questions.explanation: Filtration removes the insoluble leaves. Evaporating the filtered liquid can leave the dissolved sugar behind.
questions.difficultyRationale: It orders two methods according to whether each component is soluble or insoluble.

questions.question: A mixture contains stones, large grains and fine flour. Which approach is most suitable before any water is added?
options: Hand-pick the stones, then sieve to separate particles of different sizes
Use a magnet to dissolve the flour
Filter the dry mixture through water
questions.explanation: Hand-picking removes visible stones; sieving separates the remaining materials according to particle size.
questions.difficultyRationale: It plans two complementary physical methods based on visible differences and particle size.

questions.question: A sample of muddy water contains visible soil and dissolved salt. The aim is to obtain clear salty water, not dry salt. Which sequence is best?
options: Evaporate everything until only soil remains
Add more mud so it settles faster
Allow the soil to settle, decant the clearer liquid and filter it
Use a magnet to remove the salt
questions.explanation: Settling and decanting remove much of the soil; filtration removes remaining insoluble particles while dissolved salt stays in the water.
questions.difficultyRationale: It selects a sequence that preserves the desired dissolved substance in the liquid.

questions.question: A mixture contains rice, small stones and fine sand. Which plan is most likely to separate all three efficiently?
options: Use a magnet on all three materials
Hand-pick the stones, then sieve the rice and sand using a mesh that lets sand pass
questions.explanation: Hand-picking removes stones. A suitable sieve retains the larger rice grains while finer sand passes through.
questions.difficultyRationale: It combines visual sorting with a size-based method and considers the required mesh.

title: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which feature is shared by all living organisms?
options: They all walk from place to place
They all make their own food
questions.explanation: Living organisms carry out processes such as nutrition, growth and reproduction.

questions.question: Which organism is a vertebrate?

questions.question: Which organism is an invertebrate?

questions.question: Which plant is a climber?

questions.question: Why do cactus leaves often appear as spines?

questions.question: Which plant part usually absorbs water and minerals from soil?
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water and mineral nutrients.

questions.question: A plant with a weak stem that spreads along the ground is called a:

questions.question: Which feature helps a fish move efficiently through water?
questions.explanation: A streamlined body reduces resistance while swimming.

questions.question: Which animal is adapted to live in both water and on land?
questions.explanation: A frog is an amphibian.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which characteristic distinguishes vertebrates from invertebrates?
questions.explanation: Vertebrates possess a backbone; invertebrates do not.

questions.question: Which plant is commonly called a herb?
questions.explanation: Coriander has a soft green stem.

questions.question: A plant with a hard woody stem branching near the base is commonly a:

questions.question: Which root system is commonly found in wheat?
questions.explanation: Wheat usually has fibrous roots.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which leaf venation is commonly found in mango?
questions.explanation: Mango leaves commonly show net-like veins.

questions.question: A camel's long eyelashes and closable nostrils help mainly by:
questions.explanation: These features protect eyes and nose in sandy conditions.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Why do many desert plants have thick, fleshy stems?
options: To make the plant lighter than air
questions.explanation: Succulent stems store water for dry periods.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which habitat is most suitable for a polar bear?
questions.explanation: Polar bears are adapted to the cold Arctic.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which body covering helps many birds keep warm and supports flight?
questions.explanation: Feathers provide insulation and help with flight.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which animal group has jointed legs and an external skeleton?
questions.explanation: Arthropods have jointed appendages and an exoskeleton.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which pair contains only mammals?
questions.explanation: Dolphins and bats are mammals and feed their young with milk.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which animal breathes mainly through gills in water?
questions.explanation: Fish use gills to take oxygen from water.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which feature helps a duck move on water?
questions.explanation: Webbed feet push against water while swimming.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which statement about habitat is correct?
options: A habitat provides an organism with suitable conditions and resources
A habitat is only an animal's shelter
All organisms have the same habitat
questions.explanation: Habitats provide food, water, shelter and suitable conditions.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which is a non-living component of a forest habitat?
questions.explanation: Sunlight is abiotic; the others are living.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Why are organisms grouped into categories?
options: To show all organisms are identical
To make similarities and differences easier to study
To decide which organisms are useful
questions.explanation: Classification organises the diversity of living things.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: A plant has one main root with smaller side roots. This is a:
questions.explanation: A taproot has one main root with lateral branches.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which is an adaptation in some aquatic plants?
options: Air spaces that help the plant float
questions.explanation: Air spaces can provide buoyancy.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: A polar animal has thick fur and a layer of fat. How do these help?
questions.explanation: Fur and fat insulate the animal.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: A bird has a hooked beak and sharp claws. What food is it likely adapted to obtain?
questions.explanation: Hooked beaks and sharp claws help catch and tear prey.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which organism is a producer in a pond ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Algae photosynthesise and make food.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Why do fungi not belong to the plant group?
options: They do not make their own food by photosynthesis
questions.explanation: Fungi obtain nutrients from organic matter and lack chlorophyll.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which animal is an amphibian?
questions.explanation: Salamanders are amphibians.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: A bat flies, but it is not a bird. Which feature identifies it as a mammal?
options: It feeds its young with milk
questions.explanation: Mammals feed their young milk.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which plant is most likely a creeper?
questions.explanation: Pumpkin has a weak stem that spreads along the ground.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: A plant has parallel leaf venation. Which root type is commonly associated?
questions.explanation: Parallel venation is commonly associated with fibrous-rooted plants.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which statement about growth is most accurate?
options: All non-living things grow like organisms
Living organisms grow and develop during their life cycle
questions.explanation: Living organisms show growth and development.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Why is a polar bear's fur an adaptation?
options: It helps the animal remain warm in a cold habitat
It removes the need for food
questions.explanation: Fur provides insulation.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which pair shows an organism and a suitable habitat?
questions.explanation: Lotus is an aquatic plant.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: An animal has six legs, three body regions and antennae. Which group?
questions.explanation: Insects have three body regions and six legs.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Which feature is common to spiders but not insects?
questions.explanation: Spiders are arachnids with eight legs.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: A plant grows on another plant for support but does not take food from it. It is an:
questions.explanation: Epiphytes use another plant for support but make their own food.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: Dodder takes nutrients from a host plant. This relationship is:
questions.explanation: The parasite benefits while the host is harmed.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity

questions.question: An unknown animal has a backbone, feathers, wings and lays eggs. Which classification is best supported by all four clues?
questions.explanation: A backbone places it among vertebrates, while feathers and egg-laying are characteristic bird features.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity
questions.difficultyRationale: It combines several observable traits instead of classifying from one feature alone.

questions.question: A cactus and a water lily live in very different habitats. Which paired adaptation best explains how each suits its habitat?
options: Cactus has broad floating leaves; water lily has spines to reduce water loss
Cactus has a thick water-storing stem; water lily has broad floating leaves
Both need dry sand to survive
Water lily stores all its water in underground spines
questions.explanation: A cactus stores water and reduces loss in dry habitats; a water lily's broad floating leaves help it live on the water surface.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity
questions.difficultyRationale: It compares two organisms and links different structures to contrasting habitats.

questions.question: A pond food chain is algae → insect larvae → small fish → large fish. If the small fish population falls sharply, which immediate effect is most likely?
options: Large fish will have more food
Insect larvae may increase while large fish have less food
questions.explanation: Fewer small fish means fewer larvae are eaten, while large fish lose one of their food sources.
questions.syllabusTopic: The Living World and Its Diversity
questions.difficultyRationale: It traces two effects in opposite directions through a food chain.

questions.question: A plant produces many small, light seeds with hair-like structures. Which combination best explains how this feature helps the plant?
options: It makes the seeds heavier so they sink
It prevents the seeds from ever moving
It lets animals digest the seeds before germination
It helps air carry the seeds away from the parent plant
